focused_questions.issue: The cross-page attachment of the fol. 160b note '+ 60. Sūtasaṃhitātātparyadīpikā ... 1864.' via the line and arrow is probable, not secure.
The short vertical stroke at the gutter edge (~[330,2030]) is recorded only in page_annotations; its purpose is unknown.

The interlinear begins with a lowercase letter and its first word is not securely legible. The capitalised, certain-looking reading is not supported. Proposed literal_text: "√b. 112 (1) | Brahmagītā,/ From the Yajñavaibhavakhaṇḍa^ of the Sūtasaṃhitā\nof the Skanda Purāṇa^at.s. | 1807 : 134 : 10 : D\n[interlinear above, keyed by caret:] uparibhāga [reading?] (or Uttarabhāga)"

The bracketed '[r]' implies an editorial supply. The source shows overwritten letters within the word, not an omitted letter. Proposed literal_text: "e. 175 | Brahmajñānamahātantrarāja, otherwise called Brahmadharma, | n.d.:130:6\nBeng.\nWritten in various coloured [letters overwritten; reading?] inks."
The overwritten lines value ('2' above '14'?) cannot be read; the lines field is left empty.
The owner's name 'Vināyaka Śarma' is uncertain; the second word could be another form.

The source shows 'Pavitreṣṭi' underlined as well as touched by the wavy stroke, so the annotation should not assert that it is cancelled. Proposed annotations: ["Tick", "Ditto dash for title", "n.d. cancelled, 1723 above", "Extent and lines numerals overwritten with 8 and 11 above", "Wavy line runs through 'Contains also Mṛgāreṣṭi and' and toward 'Pavitreṣṭi', which also carries an underline; 'differs from RLM V, 1363.' uncancelled; guide line with arrowhead beneath"]
Shelfmark number read 112; middle digits loosely formed

readings.source_reading: At the target's left edge there is a trace '1864.' (~x0–110, y~880). A thin horizontal line runs from it to about x330. Separately, at about x405–530, there is a feathered arrow-like mark before the tick of b. 112 (1).
readings.evidence: Native tile [0,0]: the line from the 160b note continues across the gutter. The gap between the line end and the arrow mark leaves continuity, and therefore attachment, probable rather than secure. Matching ff.1-134 against extent 134 is a contextual inference, not a written link.
